title: Victory through weakness
english: His being defeated brought him glory rather than insult. Therefore now I conquer him through a cowardly, humble, and weak flesh, not tempting but being tempted, not striking but being struck, not killing but dying, not crucifying but being crucified, not beating but being beaten, so that the things of the victory might not be inscribed to me, but so that through the form of man the prizes might be granted to the race of men.

For this reason, therefore, I seem cowardly, so that the devil might fall like a fish upon the bait, and death might be stuck like a sparrow to the glue. Since he was wickedly deceived, for this reason he is beautifully deceived. Since he seduced the race of men through bodily pleasure, for this reason he is driven away from the race through the body. What he did, [Christ] suffers; what he did to the many, this he endures from one. But what he did, that was destruction to those who suffered it; but what I do to him, it shall be salvation to the inhabited world.

For I deceive the schemer through the body, so that, having been exposed, he may no longer be able to lead astray those whom he himself led astray through the body; he brings death, but I through it provide the resurrection. Unwillingly, he benefits the race. For through those things through which he brings death, he brings the occasion for the resurrection. The attacker of all things has become the benefactor of the inhabited world unexpectedly; for having been deceived, he benefited the inhabited world, having devised a deception beneficial to the cosmos and a trophy against his own tyranny.

Just as one sharpening a stone against rocks will not break the rock, but will crush the stone, so also the devil, having thrown death like a stone against my body as if it were a rock, did not destroy my body—for you will not see your holy one see corruption (Psalm 16:10)—but he crushed his own darts because of the opposition, being unable to endure the hardness. Let no one therefore despise my cowardice through ignorance, nor let them cast the bitter words against the Divinity.
